facts.text: That opening helicopter flyover supposedly shows Providence, Rhode Island, but the city in the shot is actually Hartford, Connecticut.
Dan O'Bannon wrote Alien and directed Return of the Living Dead. This Lovecraft adaptation was his last time in the director's chair before his death in 2009.
O'Bannon's own title was The Ancestor. Writer Brent V. Friedman's script was called Shatterbrain. Both men developed the Lovecraft story separately before the film merged their ideas.
Based on H.P. Lovecraft's novella The Case of Charles Dexter Ward. The film also played the Sitges Film Festival in Spain in 1991.
Goof alert: John calls his receptionist 'Polly' here, but later he calls her 'Holly', which is her actual name.
The budget was about $5 million, small for effects work like this. Effects artist Todd Masters's team built animatronic monsters and miniatures.
Todd Masters's effects crew won Fangoria's Chainsaw Award for their creature work on this film.
Principal photography took place in 1990 in Vancouver, British Columbia, even though the story is set in Rhode Island.
The score is by Richard Band, a prolific horror composer who also scored Re-Animator and From Beyond.
Diane O'Bannon said the film was re-cut over her husband's objections and released without his approval. His attempts at humor were edited out.
O'Bannon's first cut ran over two hours. A 2h17m work print on OFDb Filmworks' German Blu-ray restores extended dream sequences and a March/Claire romantic scene.
Chris Sarandon was Oscar-nominated for his film debut, Dog Day Afternoon. He later voiced Jack Skellington in The Nightmare Before Christmas.
Jane Sibbett, Claire here, later played Carol on Friends. John Terry, March here, later played Jack's dad on Lost.
Goof alert: the diary entry is dated Friday, October 13, 1771. October 13, 1771 was actually a Sunday.
Everyone here says 'Pawtuxet' wrong. Rhode Islanders put the stress on the second syllable, like pawTUXet.
Unlike Lovecraft, who preferred to leave horrors undescribed, the film follows Re-Animator and From Beyond in showing lots of gore.
The film was planned for a wide US release in fall 1991, but distributor Interstar went bankrupt. It went straight to video in spring 1992.
The studio briefly considered retitling the film 'Reflex.' It was also known as The Ancestor and Shatterbrain.
This was the final film released by Scotti Brothers Pictures.
Lovecraft scholars Migliore and Strysik called it 'the best serious Lovecraftian screen adaptation to date' in their book Lurker in the Lobby.
The 2017 Scream Factory Blu-ray has a commentary with the producers, writer Friedman, Todd Masters and Robert Romanus. Vinegar Syndrome put out a 4K disc in 2025.
